test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Select the correct statement for asexual reproduction in plants.

options.text: It occurs rapidly during unfavourable conditions.
It involves male and female flowers.
It is found in both lower and higher plants.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It is found in both lower and higher plants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Asexual reproduction** in plants is a process by which new individuals are produced from a **single parent** without the involvement of **gamete formation** or fusion.
 
• **Statement 1**: It occurs rapidly during **unfavourable conditions**. Asexual reproduction typically occurs when environmental conditions are **favourable** and stable, allowing the plant to colonize an area quickly. During **unfavourable conditions**, many plants prefer **sexual reproduction** or produce dormant structures like seeds or spores to ensure survival. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 2**: It involves **male and female flowers**. Flowers are the reproductive organs specifically designed for **sexual reproduction**, involving **pollination** and **fertilization**. Asexual reproduction bypasses the floral mechanism entirely. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 3**: It is found in both **lower and higher plants**. This is the defining characteristic. **Lower plants** like **Algae**, **Fungi**, and **Bryophytes** reproduce asexually through **fragmentation**, **budding**, or **zoospores**. **Higher plants** (Angiosperms) frequently reproduce asexually through **vegetative propagation** using roots, stems, or leaves. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 4**: It involves **formation of gametes**. The formation and subsequent fusion of **haploid gametes** (sperm and egg) is the hallmark of **sexual reproduction**. Asexual methods rely on **mitotic division** of somatic cells. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vegetative Propagation in Higher Plants**:
 
 
• This is a form of **asexual reproduction** where new plants are produced from vegetative parts.
 
• **Stem Tubers**: Examples include the **Potato**, where "eyes" act as nodes for new growth.
 
• **Rhizomes**: Underground stems found in **Ginger** and **Turmeric** that spread horizontally.
 
• **Runners/Stolons**: Found in **Strawberry** plants, these stems run along the ground to establish new plantlets.
 
• **Bulbs**: Short underground stems with fleshy leaves, such as in **Onions** and **Garlic**.
 
• **Adventitious Buds**: The **Bryophyllum** plant produces buds along its leaf margins that drop off to form new plants.
 
 
 
• **Asexual Methods in Lower Plants**:
 
 
• **Fragmentation**: In **Spirogyra** (an alga), the parent body breaks into smaller pieces, each growing into a new individual.
 
• **Budding**: Common in **Yeast**, where a small bulb-like projection (bud) develops and detaches.
 
• **Spore Formation**: Non-flowering plants like **Ferns** and **Mosses** produce **spores** in structures called **sporangia** which germinate under suitable conditions.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Asexual Reproduction**:
 
 
• The offspring are **genetically identical** (clones) to the parent, ensuring the preservation of **desirable traits**.
 
• It is a **faster** and more **energy-efficient** process as it does not require the plant to produce flowers, nectar, or find pollinators.
 
• It allows for the rapid **multiplication** of a species in a stable habitat.
